title: Decouple prefill serialization and simplify thread throttling to reduce host-side CPU-GPU overhead
creator: Aisha Verma
description:
Goal: reduce host-side overhead during prefill and decode by decoupling CPU serialization work from GPU dispatch, consolidating host memcopies, and replacing heavy-weight thread throttles with a deterministic token-based scheduling shim. Background: we've observed recurring spikes in host CPU utilization and long tail latency at p99 during multi-tenant bursts. Root causes include serialized prefill steps that block worker threads, redundant memcpy fanout to staging buffers, and contention in the threadpool when many small sessions are scheduled concurrently. Proposed approach:

1) Prefill serialization decoupling: introduce a lockless work-queue boundary between request assembly and GPU dispatch. The CPU-side serializer will produce compact work descriptors (pointer + length + metadata) which are enqueued to a single-producer multi-consumer ring; GPU dispatcher workers pop descriptors and perform the minimal GPU submission. This keeps per-request CPU work bounded and avoids blocking the network/IO threads.

2) Memcopy consolidation: implement a coalescing layer that merges small host->staging memcpys into batched scatter-gather submissions when requests target contiguous staging slabs. Add heuristics to prefer pinned pages for large contiguous writes and fall back to pooled ephemeral buffers for tiny writes.

3) Thread throttle simplification: replace the current reactive thread parking/unparking system with a token-bucket style scheduler for the worker pool. Tokens represent dispatch slots and are replenished on a steady schedule plus a small burst allowance. This reduces pathological wakeups and flapping while preserving headroom for tail-latency-sensitive requests.

4) Kernel hinting integration: attach lightweight kernel-selection hints to work descriptors (e.g., attention-optimized path vs generic) so the dispatcher can prefer pre-warmed kernels for predicted runtime shapes and avoid expensive kernel probes during hot paths.

Trade-offs: the ring buffer adds a small bounded memory overhead and introduces one extra indirection per request; token-bucket may slightly reduce peak throughput under perfectly uniform load but improves latency stability.

Outcome: aim for measurable reductions in host CPU sys time, reduced memcpy amplification, and lower p99 prefill-to-dispatch latency.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Reduce host CPU user+sys attributable to prefill/dispatch pipeline by >= 30% on representative multi-tenant benchmark (same traffic mix as perf-2026-02).
2) Reduce memcpy bandwidth amplification (measured as total host memcpy bytes / logical input bytes) by >= 40% for small-request workloads.
3) Improve p99 prefill-to-first-dispatch latency from current baseline to at least 35% lower on cluster staging environment.
4) No regression in throughput for large-batch offline workloads (<= 5% throughput decrease).
5) All changes covered by unit/integration tests and gated behind a runtime flag for canary rollout.
6) Observability: add per-descriptor counters (queued, merged, dropped) and threadpool token metrics to Console dashboards.
updates: 2026-02-22: Spike completed — evaluated ring-buffer vs MPMC queue; ring buffer chosen for low-latency single-producer common case. Latency microbench attached.

2026-02-26: Design review with Platform and Runtime teams. PM requested explicit canary plan and backward-compatible failure mode. Decided to fall back to legacy path if descriptor processing fails three times consecutively.
2026-03-02: Prototype implemented: lockless ring + descriptor struct. End-to-end microbench shows 28% host CPU reduction for 64B requests, memcopy bytes reduced by 34% in best-case contiguous layout.
2026-03-06: Integration note — attention kernel hinting requires small API surface change (Descriptor.hint). Runtime tests show kernel probe latency reduced by ~0.9ms on warm path.

2026-03-10: Started canary rollout to staging cluster: 10% of traffic using new path. Observed token-bucket eliminates most thread wakeup spikes; p99 latency improved in canary by 22% so far. Two follow-ups added for edge-case buffer exhaustion handling.
